Tuga A6 vs Tuga WH6

For anyone who wants a rugged device that fits a pocket or belt holster and is torn between Android and Windows. The short answer: buy the Tuga A6 at £349 unless a Windows-only program or a network drive is on your must-have list, in which case the Tuga WH6 at £699 is the one to buy.

Verdict

The short answer

The Tuga A6 is the better buy unless you need Windows. It costs £349 against £699 for the WH6, a gap of £350, and on the things a pocket device is judged on it holds its own or leads: sealed to IP67 against the WH6's IP65, a 5050mAh battery against 4000mAh, both removable, 277g against 470g, and a Zebra 2D scan engine built in as standard. Both are rated for 1.5 metre drops and both have 4G LTE, dual-band Wi-Fi 5 and NFC. If your work runs on apps and the web (scanning, job sheets, photos, proof of delivery, messaging), there is little reason to pay the extra.

Pay the £350 when one thing is non-negotiable: a Windows desktop program or a network drive that you need in the field. The WH6 runs Windows 11 IoT on an Intel Celeron N5100 with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, against 4GB and 64GB on the A6, so it can run Windows desktop software, and it has a USB-A port for connecting instruments and peripherals directly. It also lists MIL-STD-810H, which the A6 does not, a -20°C to 60°C rating against -20°C to 50°C, and an 8MP autofocus rear camera against 13MP on the A6. Before you order, check that your specific program runs on it and is usable on a 6.5 inch screen. If one program is the sticking point, tell us what it is and we will point you to the right device.

On scanning, the gap widens. The A6 has an integrated Zebra 2D scan engine with two side scan keys at £349. To get a scan engine on the WH6 you need the WH6 with Barcode Scanner at £779, £80 more than the standard WH6 and £430 more than the A6. On warranty, both include 12 months, and the paid 3-Year Warranty is £65 on the A6 and £89 on the WH6. Delivery is free to UK addresses in 7 to 10 working days on either, with no VAT to add. For the wider question, read our Android vs Windows guide; for drivers and pickers, the logistics page goes through both devices.

Choose the Tuga A6 if

  • Every program you use runs as an app or in a browser, and you would rather keep £350.
  • You scan barcodes and want the scanner built in: the A6 has an integrated Zebra 2D scan engine at £349, against £779 for the WH6 with Barcode Scanner.
  • The device gets rained on or dropped in water: IP67, which covers immersion, against IP65, which covers water jets.
  • You carry it all day and want the lighter device: 277g against 470g.
  • You want the bigger battery of the two, still removable: 5050mAh against 4000mAh, with dual SIM 4G for patchy coverage.

Choose the Tuga WH6 if

  • You need a Windows desktop program or a network drive on site, and you have checked it runs on the WH6.
  • You plug into instruments or peripherals over USB-A and do not want an £8 OTG adapter.
  • You want more memory and storage: 8GB of RAM and 128GB, expandable to 512GB, against 4GB and 64GB, expandable to 256GB, on the A6.
  • You want a desk cradle to drop it into: the WH6 Charging Cradle (£79) is listed for the WH6, and no dock or cradle is listed for the A6.
  • Your team already works in Windows and you want a Windows 11 handheld alongside the office PCs, once you have checked your software on it.
Specification

What is different

Every line comes from the two specification sheets, the same figures as the product pages. Rows where the A6 and WH6 differ are tinted.

  • The WH6 costs £350 more: £699 against £349 for the A6.
  • The A6 is lighter by 193g: 277g against 470g for the WH6.
  • The WH6 has the bigger screen: 6.5 inch against 6 inch on the A6.
  • The A6 has the higher resolution: 2160 x 1080 against 720 x 1600 on the WH6.
  • Brightness is not listed for the A6; the WH6 lists 400 nits.
  • The A6 has the bigger battery: 5050mAh removable against 4000mAh on the WH6.
  • The A6 is sealed to IP67 and the WH6 to IP65.
  • Drop standard is not listed for the A6; the WH6 lists MIL-STD-810H.
  • The A6 runs Android 15; the WH6 runs Windows 11 IoT.
  • Connectivity: 4G LTE, dual-band Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.1, NFC on the A6 vs 4G LTE, dual-band Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.0, NFC, GPS + GLONASS on the WH6.

Identical on both: drop spec (1.5m).

FAQ

Questions about the A6 and WH6

Only if you need Windows. The WH6 runs Windows 11 IoT, so it can run Windows desktop software and access network drives, and it has twice the RAM and storage. The A6 runs Android 15, so a Windows desktop program will not install on it. If your software has an Android app or runs in a browser, the A6 is the cheaper place to start, with better sealing, a larger removable battery, less weight and a barcode scanner built in, but check your own apps on it first. Do not assume a program that runs on an office PC will suit a 6.5 inch handheld: check it on the device, or tell us what it is.

The A6 is better sealed; the WH6 lists more beyond that. The A6 is IP67, which covers dust and immersion, while the WH6 is IP65, which covers dust and water jets but not immersion. Both list a 1.5 metre drop rating. The WH6 also lists MIL-STD-810H, which the A6 does not, and is rated from -20°C to 60°C against -20°C to 50°C on the A6, so for a van cab in summer the WH6 has the higher listed figure. Our IP rating guide explains what each number is tested for.

Both are removable, so a charged spare can swap in without waiting on a cable. The A6 has 5050mAh and the WH6 4000mAh, so the A6 starts the day with about a quarter more capacity. Spare batteries are not listed as an accessory for either, so ask us before you plan around one. For charging, the WH6 Charging Cradle (£79) fits the WH6, and the 12V DC Car Charger (£26) fits both. The A6 has charging contacts on the body, but no dock or cradle is listed for it, so it charges over USB-C.

Only if you need Windows as well as scanning. The WH6 with Barcode Scanner has an integrated 2D scan engine and costs £779, £80 more than the standard WH6. The A6 has a Zebra 2D scan engine and two side scan keys as standard at £349, £430 less. If your scanning app runs on Android, start with the A6 and test it with the labels you actually read, scuffed and in poor light. If scans have to go straight into a Windows program, the WH6 with Barcode Scanner is the one. Our guide to built-in barcode scanners covers when a scan engine pays over a camera app.
